item.title: Lautoka man in custody after methamphetamine seizure
item.description: A 37-year-old man is in custody for the alleged unlawful possession of methamphetamine following a joint raid in Lautoka. Assistant Commissioner of Police Operations Kasiano Vusonilawe says the raid was conducted by the Joint Task Force, comprising officers from the Fiji Police Force and the Republic of Fiji Military Forces, at the suspect's home yesterday afternoon.
item.content:encoded:
A 37-year-old man is in custody for the alleged unlawful possession of methamphetamine following a joint raid in Lautoka.

Assistant Commissioner of Police Operations Kasiano Vusonilawe says the raid was conducted by the Joint Task Force, comprising officers from the Fiji Police Force and the Republic of Fiji Military Forces, at the suspect's home yesterday afternoon.

A K9 unit was deployed at the suspect's residence, where plastic packets containing crystals and drug-smoking paraphernalia were seized.

ACP Vusonilawe says analysis conducted on the seized substances confirmed they were methamphetamine.

He is urging members of the public to share information on drug-related activities by calling the 1681 toll-free number.

item.title: 264 earthquakes recorded in Fiji region in July
item.description: A total of 264 earthquakes were recorded across the Fiji region last month, with magnitudes ranging from 1.2 to 5.9. According to Fiji Seismology, a high concentration of shallow earthquakes was recorded in the northern region of Fiji, particularly around Vanua Levu, extending from the northern Yasawa Islands to Cikobia Island along the Fiji Fracture Zone.
item.content:encoded:
A total of 264 earthquakes were recorded across the Fiji region last month, with magnitudes ranging from 1.2 to 5.9.

According to Fiji Seismology, a high concentration of shallow earthquakes was recorded in the northern region of Fiji, particularly around Vanua Levu, extending from the northern Yasawa Islands to Cikobia Island along the Fiji Fracture Zone.

Fiji Seismology says this level of activity is expected for the fault zone.

The report also highlights that deep earthquakes, between 300 and 600 kilometres below the surface, were concentrated east of Fiji, particularly beneath the Lau Basin, indicating subduction-related activity as the Pacific Plate moves beneath the Indo-Australian Plate.

Other areas that recorded shallow, minor seismic activity include Kadavu Island, which is associated with the Hunter Fracture Zone, southeast Viti Levu, and parts of inland Vanua Levu.

Members of the public are encouraged to report any felt earthquakes through Fiji Seismology's official Facebook page, by calling 338 1611 , or by emailing mrd_seismology@yahoo.com .

item.title: PM to lead sugar industry consultations with farmers in Vanua Levu
item.description: Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka will lead Parliament's Special Committee on the Sugar Industry as it begins public consultations in Vanua Levu today, meeting directly with sugarcane farmers to discuss the future of Fiji's sugar industry. The consultations will give farmers the opportunity to share their experiences, raise challenges affecting their farms, and put forward practical solutions to help
item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka will lead Parliament's Special Committee on the Sugar Industry as it begins public consultations in Vanua Levu today, meeting directly with sugarcane farmers to discuss the future of Fiji's sugar industry.

The consultations will give farmers the opportunity to share their experiences, raise challenges affecting their farms, and put forward practical solutions to help revive and strengthen the industry.

The first consultation will be held from 2pm to 4pm today at the Sanatan Hall in Seaqaqa.

A second consultation will take place from 10am to 12pm tomorrow at the Vanua Levu Arya Samaj Hall in Namara followed by a tour of the Labasa Sugar Mill from 12.10pm to 1pm.

Farmers are encouraged to participate in these consultations to raise their concerns and also come up with solutions.

The Coalition Government says it remains committed to working alongside farmers to improve productivity, strengthen the sugar industry, protect livelihoods and secure a more sustainable future for cane-growing communities across Fiji.

item.title: Kadavu Chiefs visit Naboro to support inmate reintegration
item.description: A delegation from the Kadavu Provincial Council, led by Roko Tui Kadavu Joji Banuve, visited the Naboro Corrections Complex on Tuesday to strengthen support for inmates preparing to return to their communities. The delegation included 15 high chiefs from Kadavu, who travelled to the facility following last week's Kadavu Day Solevu in Suva.
item.content:encoded:
A delegation from the Kadavu Provincial Council, led by Roko Tui Kadavu Joji Banuve, visited the Naboro Corrections Complex on Tuesday to strengthen support for inmates preparing to return to their communities.

The delegation included 15 high chiefs from Kadavu, who travelled to the facility following last week's Kadavu Day Solevu in Suva.

The chiefs held talanoa and question-and-answer sessions with inmates from Kadavu, discussed challenges they may face upon release, and explored ways the Vanua could assist with their reintegration.

The Council also assessed the support and resources needed to help former inmates rebuild their lives and establish sustainable livelihoods when they return to the island.

Roko Tui says the Council and the Vanua have a cultural and moral responsibility to support those seeking a second chance.

He says the visit provided an opportunity to better understand the needs of inmates and reassure them that they would not be left to face reintegration alone.

The Fiji Corrections Service welcomed the initiative, describing it as an example of the important role communities play in successful rehabilitation.

Supervisor Southern Division Alevio Turaga says reintegration cannot be achieved by the Corrections Service alone and requires the support and leadership of the Vanua to help former inmates successfully return to society.

FSC says community acceptance is essential in reducing reoffending and building safer, more secure communities.

item.title: Charan Jeath Singh returns as Sugar Minister
item.description: Charan Jeath Singh has returned as Sugar Minister after Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka reversed an earlier Cabinet allocation that placed responsibility for the portfolio under Agriculture Minister Tomasi Tunabuna. Singh says he was informed of the decision in an email from the Prime Minister on Monday night.
item.content:encoded:
Charan Jeath Singh has returned as Sugar Minister after Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka reversed an earlier Cabinet allocation that placed responsibility for the portfolio under Agriculture Minister Tomasi Tunabuna.

Singh says he was informed of the decision in an email from the Prime Minister on Monday night.

While speaking to fijivillage News, Singh says he will continue the work he had started in the sugar industry and ensure it moves forward.

The Minister has thanked the Prime Minister for restoring the Sugar portfolio to him.

He is expected to formally take up the portfolio next week.
